title: CX-MT046-ExecLaneCompatRouting
clause: Keep codex exec --json lane green; adapter-selection policy (app-server when SteerMidTurn required); exec resume; --output-schema for hsk.mt_signal@1

scope.summary:
GOAL: Keep the existing one-shot `codex exec --json` lane fully working alongside the new app-server lane, add the adapter-selection policy that routes work between the two (app-server preferred whenever SteerMidTurn is required; exec for fire-and-forget), wire `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>` / `--last` for one-shot continuation, and bind `--output-schema <json-schema-file>` so exec-lane runs emit hsk.mt_signal@1 structured exits (MT-121 contract) as the final message.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New file src/backend/handshake_core/src/model_runtime/cloud/codex_app_server/routing.rs (adapter-selection policy + exec-continuation + output-schema binding helpers); regression tests pinning the exec-lane preset invariants; a small, additive wiring change in swarm_orchestration/production_factory.rs so the factory consults the selection policy when both adapters are available. NO behavior change to official_cli_bridge.rs validation or cli_bridge_runtime.rs streaming - the exec lane's contract is frozen by regression tests in this MT.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. EXEC-LANE FREEZE (regression tests). The exec lane's validated preset stays exactly as enforced today by official_cli_bridge.rs validate_cli_preset (lines 963-1015): args_template starts with `exec` (984-988), contains `--json` (989-993), output_format JsonStream (979-983), single standalone `{prompt}` as final arg (994-1013), Windows entrypoint must be the verified codex.cmd npm shim (967-978), and model binding via `--model {model}` or `-m {model}` (validate_model_binding lines 1017-1059). This MT adds regression tests that pin each invariant so no CX-group change can silently break the one-shot lane; JSONL stdout continues to flow through cli_bridge_runtime.rs into parse_codex_line (agent_activity.rs line 284) unchanged.
2. ADAPTER-SELECTION POLICY. routing.rs exposes select_codex_adapter(requirements) -> CodexAdapterChoice { AppServer | Exec } with typed requirements: { needs_steer_mid_turn, needs_interrupt, needs_fork, needs_resume_thread, fire_and_forget, structured_exit_required }. Policy (deterministic, table-driven, unit-tested): (a) needs_steer_mid_turn or needs_interrupt or needs_fork -> AppServer (capabilities only that lane advertises via the MT-042/MT-003 snapshot); (b) fire_and_forget with no steering needs -> Exec (cheapest, no persistent child); (c) needs_resume without steering -> Exec with `codex exec resume` when a prior exec session id is on record, else AppServer thread/resume; (d) conflicting/unsatisfiable requirement sets return a typed UnroutableRequirements error - never a silent downgrade that discards a required capability. The chosen lane is recorded (FR, via the MT-045 seam) with the requirement set that drove the choice, so routing is auditable. A session runs on EXACTLY ONE codex lane at a time (exclusivity guard; prevents the MT-045 double-recording hazard).
3. EXEC CONTINUATION. Wire `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>` (and `--last` only as an explicit operator convenience, never as an implicit default) for one-shot continuation: the exec lane records the codex session id from its JSONL events (thread.started/session metadata; sessions persist under ~/.codex/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/), persists it alongside the run record, and a continuation request renders a resume argv instead of a fresh prompt argv. The resume argv must still satisfy the frozen preset invariants that apply (exec-first, --json, JsonStream, prompt placement per the resume grammar) - extend the preset validation ONLY through additive, separately-tested code paths in routing.rs (a resume-args builder validated against the same rules), not by loosening validate_cli_preset.
4. STRUCTURED EXIT BINDING (MT-121). For MT-governed exec runs, bind `--output-schema <json-schema-file>`: routing.rs materializes the hsk.mt_signal@1 JSON schema (from the MT-121 contract artifact - consumed, not redefined) to a temp file with a stable content hash, appends `--output-schema <path>` to the rendered argv, and pairs it with `--output-last-message <path>` capture so the structured final message is read back from a file (robust against interleaved stdout), parsed, and validated against hsk.mt_signal@1. Parse/validation failure of the final message is a typed StructuredExitInvalid outcome recorded against the run - never treated as a successful exit. stdin-prompt mode (`codex exec -`) may be used for long prompts; if used, it must remain compatible with the frozen preset validation (documented decision in code comments + test).
5. FACTORY WIRING. production_factory.rs: when building Codex runtimes, consult select_codex_adapter with the request's requirements; keep CliBridgeCloudRuntimeBuilder (line 507) as the exec-lane builder unchanged; the app-server lane is selected through its own builder (MT-041..043 surface). The wiring change is additive and behind the policy call; existing non-Codex lanes are untouched.

STEP-BY-STEP IMPLEMENTATION:
1. Read validate_cli_preset/validate_model_binding (official_cli_bridge.rs 963-1059), the rendered-argv path, cli_bridge_runtime.rs streaming, the MT-121 hsk.mt_signal@1 contract, and the MT-042 capability snapshot in the implementation worktree.
2. Author the exec-lane regression test module pinning every invariant in spec item 1 (reuse existing test fixtures at official_cli_bridge.rs ~3342-3468 as the pattern).
3. Author routing.rs: requirements type, decision table, exclusivity guard, FR-recorded choice; unit tests for every table row + UnroutableRequirements + exclusivity.
4. Implement exec session-id capture + persistence + the resume-args builder with its own validation tests.
5. Implement the output-schema binding per spec item 4: schema materialization (hash-stable temp file), argv extension, --output-last-message capture + parse + validate, StructuredExitInvalid path; tests with valid, invalid, and missing final messages.
6. Wire the factory consultation per spec item 5; run the FULL existing official_cli_bridge + cli_bridge_runtime test suites to prove zero exec-lane regression.
7. Run proof targets; record outputs.
forbidden_paths: src/frontend/** (no GUI work in this MT)
MT-121 mt_signal contract artifacts (consume the schema; do not redefine)
acceptance_criteria: Exec-lane regression tests pin all preset invariants (exec-first, --json, JsonStream, standalone trailing {prompt}, Windows codex.cmd shim, --model/-m binding) and the full existing official_cli_bridge + cli_bridge_runtime suites pass unchanged (proof).

select_codex_adapter routes: steer/interrupt/fork requirements -> AppServer; pure fire-and-forget -> Exec; resume-without-steering -> Exec resume when a session id exists else AppServer thread/resume; unsatisfiable sets -> typed UnroutableRequirements (table-driven tests, one per row).
No silent capability downgrade: a requirement the chosen lane cannot honor is impossible by construction (test asserts choice always satisfies requirements).
Lane exclusivity: one session cannot hold both codex lanes concurrently (test).
Every routing decision is recorded with its driving requirement set via the MT-045 seam (test).

Exec continuation: session id captured from run events, persisted, and a continuation renders `codex exec resume <SESSION_ID>` argv that passes the resume-args builder validation; --last is only reachable via explicit operator flag (tests).

hsk.mt_signal@1 binding: MT-governed exec runs append --output-schema with the materialized schema and capture the final message via --output-last-message; valid message parses + validates; invalid/missing message yields typed StructuredExitInvalid, never success (tests).
production_factory consults the policy additively; non-Codex lanes and the exec builder body are untouched (mechanical diff criterion).

implementation_notes: The exec lane is production surface for existing WPs; the freeze-by-regression-test approach means any future preset change must consciously update BOTH the validator and these pins.
`--output-schema` constrains the FINAL message shape; intermediate JSONL events are unaffected and still feed parse_codex_line recording.

Schema materialization must be deterministic (stable hash in filename) so concurrent runs share/read identical schema files without races; write-once semantics, scratch/temp root per project portability policy (no hardcoded absolute paths).

`--ignore-user-config` should be considered for governed exec runs so user-level codex config cannot alter governed behavior; wire it as a policy flag with a test, defaulting to the current lane behavior (do not silently change existing runs).
Sandbox flags (--sandbox workspace-write | danger-full-access) remain owned by the existing exec-lane config/escalation policy; routing.rs must pass them through untouched.

UnroutableRequirements exists for honesty: e.g. structured_exit_required + needs_steer_mid_turn is satisfiable only if the app-server lane exposes an equivalent structured-exit path via MT-121's app-server binding - if it does not at implementation time, that combination is unroutable-typed, not silently degraded.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Headless routing/compat MT: no operator-visible surface changed; visual verification = TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004 (recorded routing decisions).

target_entries: Codex lanes: when work runs on app-server vs exec (the selection policy, in operator terms), lane exclusivity, and how to read recorded routing decisions
Codex exec lane: one-shot continuation (resume <SESSION_ID> / explicit --last) and structured exits (hsk.mt_signal@1 via --output-schema)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Routing decisions + structured-exit outcomes are FR business events via the MT-045 seam.
Recorded DEFERRED-with-reason if internal_diagnostics is not present in the implementation worktree at claim time; never silently skipped.
Routing is in-process policy; child liveness concerns belong to the lanes themselves (MT-041/exec spawner); recorded, never silently skipped.

risk_if_missed: Either the new lane cannibalizes the proven one-shot lane (regressions in existing WP automation) or steering-required work lands on the exec lane and silently cannot be steered; MT-governed runs lose structured hsk.mt_signal@1 exits on the exec path.

risks: RISK-1: Silent capability downgrade - routing sends steer-required work to the exec lane and the steering just never happens (worst failure of the WP: looks green, cannot steer).
RISK-2: Exec-lane regression - CX-group changes loosen or bypass the frozen preset validation, breaking the production one-shot lane other WPs depend on.
RISK-3: Structured-exit spoofing/miss - treating an unvalidated or missing final message as a successful MT signal corrupts the MT-121 signal contract downstream.
RISK-4: Implicit --last resume - resuming "the last session" implicitly can attach a governed run to an unrelated interactive session of the operator.
RISK-5: Dual-lane session - one session holding both lanes concurrently double-records and double-executes.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): choice_always_satisfies_requirements invariant test + UnroutableRequirements instead of downgrade; routing decision recorded with requirements.
CTRL-2 (RISK-2): official_cli_bridge.rs/cli_bridge_runtime.rs are forbidden paths; full existing suites are proof targets; new regression pins for every invariant.
CTRL-3 (RISK-3): --output-last-message file capture + schema validation; StructuredExitInvalid typed outcome; tests for invalid AND missing messages.
CTRL-4 (RISK-4): --last reachable only behind an explicit operator flag; test proves no implicit path.
CTRL-5 (RISK-5): Session-scoped exclusivity guard with concurrent test (HBR-SWARM-001-adjacent hazard).
